sentences.en: Good morning, everyone.
sentences.zh: 大家早上好。

sentences.en: In our last lecture, I was talking about language as part of our semiotic system.
sentences.zh: 上一讲中，我谈到语言是我们符号系统的一部分。

sentences.en: And today, I’m going to move on to another topic, that is, the modes of language.
sentences.zh: 今天我要转向另一个话题，也就是语言的表达方式。

sentences.en: As you may know, messages are transmitted in human language most frequently through two primary modes: speech and writing.
sentences.zh: 大家可能知道，人类语言传递信息最常用的两种基本方式是口语和书面语。

sentences.en: Well, you know there is also a third mode which is not that frequently used as speech and writing.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有第三种方式，只是没有口语和书面语那么常用。

sentences.en: The third mode is called signing, which is used by deaf people.
sentences.zh: 第三种方式叫手语，是失聪人士使用的。

sentences.en: But in today’s lecture, we will just focus on speech and writing and the specific features of these two modes.
sentences.zh: 不过，今天我们只讨论口语和书面语，以及这两种表达方式各自的特点。

sentences.en: In linguistics, it is commonly noted that speech is primary and writing secondary.
sentences.zh: 在语言学中，人们通常认为口语是首要的，书面语是次要的。

sentences.en: Linguists take this position because all languages are spoken except those dead languages such as Latin, which now exist only in written form.
sentences.zh: 语言学家持这种观点，是因为除了拉丁语这类如今只以书面形式存在的死语言之外，所有语言都有口语形式。

w.m: phr.死语言；已无母语使用者的语言

sentences.en: All children will naturally acquire the spoken version of a language if they are exposed to it.
sentences.zh: 只要接触到一种语言，所有儿童都会自然习得它的口语形式。

sentences.en: They acquire the spoken form of their mother tongue during the formative period of language acquisition.
sentences.zh: 他们在语言习得的关键成长阶段，掌握母语的口语形式。

sentences.en: However, to become literate, a child will need some kind of formal schooling in reading and writing.
sentences.zh: 然而，要具备读写能力，儿童就需要接受某种正规的读写教育。

sentences.en: In many respects, we might call speech “primary” and writing “secondary”.
sentences.zh: 在许多方面，我们或许可以称口语为“首要的”，称书面语为“次要的”。

sentences.en: It implies that writing has a second-class status when compared with speech.
sentences.zh: 但这会暗示，相较于口语，书面语的地位低人一等。

sentences.en: In fact, it is more accurate to view the two modes as having different but complementary roles.
sentences.zh: 事实上，更准确的看法是：这两种方式发挥着不同但互补的作用。

sentences.en: For instance, in most legal systems, while an oral contract is legally binding, a written contract is preferred.
sentences.zh: 例如，在大多数法律制度中，虽然口头合同具有法律约束力，人们仍更倾向于书面合同。

sentences.en: The reason is simple.
sentences.zh: 原因很简单。

sentences.en: Unlike speech, writing provides a permanent record of the contract.
sentences.zh: 与口语不同，书面语可以为合同留下永久记录。

sentences.en: Thus, if the terms of the contract are disputed, the written record of the contract can be consulted and interpreted.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果人们对合同条款发生争议，就可以查阅并解释合同的书面记录。

sentences.en: Disputes over an oral contract will involve one person’s recollection of the contract versus another person’s.
sentences.zh: 而围绕口头合同的争议，会变成双方各执一词，比较各自对合同内容的记忆。

sentences.en: While writing may be the preferred mode for a contract, in many other contexts, speech will be more appropriate.
sentences.zh: 虽然书面语可能更适合订立合同，但在其他许多情境中，口语会更加合适。

sentences.en: Because the most common type of speech – face-to-face conversations – is highly interactive, this mode is well suited to many social contexts, such as casual conversations over lunch, business transactions in a grocery store, discussions between students and teachers in a classroom.
sentences.zh: 最常见的口语形式——面对面交谈——具有很强的互动性，因此很适用于许多社交情境，例如午餐时闲聊、杂货店里的买卖交流，以及课堂上师生之间的讨论。

sentences.en: And in these contexts, interactive dialogues have many advantages over writing.
sentences.zh: 在这些情境中，互动式对话比书面语具有许多优势。

sentences.en: For instance, individuals engaged in conversation can ask for immediate clarification if there is a question about something said; in a letter to a friend, in contrast, such immediacy is lacking.
sentences.zh: 例如，交谈者如果对刚听到的内容有疑问，可以立即要求澄清；相比之下，给朋友写信就缺少这种即时性。

sentences.en: When speaking to one another, speakers are face-to-face and can therefore see how individuals react to what is said; on the other hand, writing creates distance between writer and reader, preventing the writer from getting any immediate reaction from the reader.
sentences.zh: 交谈时，说话双方彼此面对面，因此能看到对方对话语的反应；而写作使作者与读者之间存在距离，作者无法得到读者的即时反馈。

sentences.en: Speech is oral, thus making it possible to use intonation to emphasize words or phrases and express emotion.
sentences.zh: 口语通过声音表达，因此可以运用语调来强调词语或短语，并传达情感。

sentences.en: Of course, one might say that writing has punctuation.
sentences.zh: 当然，有人可能会说，书面语有标点符号。

sentences.en: Well, it can express only a small proportion of the features that intonation has.
sentences.zh: 但标点符号只能表达语调所能体现的一小部分特征。

sentences.en: Because speech is created “on-line,” it is produced quickly and easily.
sentences.zh: 因为口语是在表达过程中即时生成的，所以产生得既快又容易。

w.m: adv.即时地；边表达边生成地

sentences.en: This may result in many “ungrammatical” constructions, but rarely do these rough sentences cause miscommunications.
sentences.zh: 这可能产生许多“不符合语法”的结构，但这些不够严整的句子很少造成沟通障碍。

sentences.en: You know, if there is a misunderstanding, it can be easily corrected.
sentences.zh: 即使发生误解，也很容易纠正。

sentences.en: On the contrary, writing is much more deliberate.
sentences.zh: 相反，书面表达需要经过更多深思熟虑。

sentences.en: It requires planning, editing and thus taking much more time to produce on the part of the writer.
sentences.zh: 它要求写作者进行构思和修改，因此需要花费更多时间才能完成。

sentences.en: Because of all of these characteristics of writing, if an individual desires a casual, intimate encounter with a friend, he or she is more likely to meet personally than write a letter.
sentences.zh: 由于书面语的这些特点，如果一个人想与朋友轻松、亲近地交流，通常更愿意亲自见面，而不是写信。

sentences.en: In this case, writing a letter to a friend might turn out to be too formal.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，给朋友写信反而可能显得过于正式。

sentences.en: Of course, in today’s world, the highly developed technology has made such encounters possible with “instant messaging” over a computer or a smart phone.
sentences.zh: 当然，在当今世界，高度发展的技术让人们可以通过电脑或智能手机上的“即时通信”来进行这类交流。

sentences.en: And if someone wishes to have such an encounter with a friend living many miles away, then this kind of on-line written “chat” can mimic a face-to-face conversation.
sentences.zh: 如果想与相隔很远的朋友交流，这种网上文字“聊天”就可以模拟面对面的交谈。

sentences.en: But because such conversations are a hybrid of speech and writing, they still lack the intimacy and immediacy of a face-to-face conversation.
sentences.zh: 但由于这种交谈是口语和书面语的混合形式，它仍然缺少面对面交流的亲近感和即时性。

sentences.en: While speech and writing are often viewed as discrete modes, it is important for us to note that there is a continuum between speech and writing.
sentences.zh: 虽然口语和书面语往往被视为彼此独立的表达方式，但我们必须注意，两者之间存在一个连续体。

sentences.en: While speech is in general more interactive than writing, various kinds of spoken and written English display various degrees of interactivity.
sentences.zh: 总体来说，口语比书面语更具互动性，不过，不同类型的英语口语和书面语所呈现的互动程度也各不相同。

sentences.en: For instance, various linguistic markers of interactive discourse, such as first- and second-person pronouns, contractions, and private verbs such as think and feel, occurred very frequently in telephone and face-to-face conversations but less frequently in spontaneous speeches, interviews, and broadcasts.
sentences.zh: 例如，第一、第二人称代词、缩略形式，以及think和feel这类表示内心活动的动词，都是互动话语的语言标记；它们在电话和面对面交谈中出现得非常频繁，在即兴演讲、访谈和广播中则少一些。

sentences.en: In addition, some kinds of writing, such as academic prose and official documents, exhibited few markers of interactive discourse.
sentences.zh: 此外，学术文章和官方文件等某些书面文本中，互动话语的标记很少。

sentences.en: But other kinds of written texts, particularly personal letters, ranked higher on the scale of interactivity than many of the spoken texts.
sentences.zh: 但另一些书面文本，特别是私人信件，其互动程度高于许多口语文本。

sentences.en: In other words, how language is structured depends less on whether it is spoken or written but more on how it is being used.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，语言的组织方式与其说取决于口头还是书面形式，不如说取决于它如何被使用。

sentences.en: For example, a personal letter, even though it is written, will contain linguistic features marking interactivity because the writer of a letter wishes to interact with the receiver of the letter.
sentences.zh: 例如，私人信件虽然是书面的，却含有体现互动性的语言特征，因为写信者希望与收信者交流。

sentences.en: On the other hand, in an interview, the goal is not to interact necessarily but to get information from the person being interviewed.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，访谈的目的未必是互动，而是从受访者那里获取信息。

sentences.en: Therefore, though interviews are spoken, they have fewer markers of interactivity and contain more features typically associated with written texts.
sentences.zh: 因此，访谈虽然采用口语形式，互动标记却较少，反而含有更多通常与书面文本相关的特征。

sentences.en: OK, to sum up, we have been dealing with the modes of language in today’s lecture.
sentences.zh: 好，总结一下，今天这堂课我们讨论了语言的表达方式。

sentences.en: The two most frequently used modes are speech and writing.
sentences.zh: 最常用的两种方式是口语和书面语。

sentences.en: As two different modes of language, speech and writing have their own characteristics.
sentences.zh: 作为两种不同的语言表达方式，口语和书面语各有特点。

sentences.en: Speech is a preferred mode in many social contexts where interactivity is needed.
sentences.zh: 在许多需要互动的社交情境中，口语是更合适的方式。

sentences.en: Of course, when a formal, stable record is preferred, writing should be an appropriate mode.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果需要正式、稳定的记录，书面语应该是适宜的表达方式。

sentences.en: Finally, I have also emphasized that there is a continuum between speech and writing.
sentences.zh: 最后，我也强调了口语与书面语之间存在一个连续体。

sentences.en: In the following lecture, we will concentrate on the linguistic structures of language.
sentences.zh: 下一讲，我们将重点讨论语言的结构。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢大家。

sentences.en: Good evening, everybody.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 大家晚上好。

sentences.en: Despite new promise of aid, international leaders provided disheartening assessments of the current battle against Ebola.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 尽管有了新的援助承诺，国际领导人对当前抗击埃博拉疫情的形势仍给出了令人沮丧的评估。

sentences.en: The head of the World Bank said the international community—community had—quote—“failed miserably” in its initial response.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 世界银行行长说，国际社会——国际社会在最初的应对中，引用他的话说——“败得很惨”。

sentences.en: The director of the Center for Disease Control said the situation reminded him of the early days of the AIDS epidemic.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 美国疾病控制中心主任说，这种情况让他想起了艾滋病疫情初起时的情形。

sentences.en: We get our own assessment from one of the few nongovernmental groups treating patients in West Africa.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 接下来，我们来听听在西非救治病人的少数几个非政府组织之一，如何评估当前形势。

sentences.en: International Medical Corps has built a treatment clinic in Liberia and is constructing other facilities in both Liberia and Sierra Leone.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 国际医疗队已经在利比里亚建起一家治疗诊所，并正在利比里亚和塞拉利昂建设其他医疗设施。

sentences.en: Its president and CEO, Mary Johnson, joins me now.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 该组织的总裁兼首席执行官玛丽·约翰逊现在来到我们节目中。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 感谢您参加我们的节目。

sentences.en: Thank you, Jack.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，杰克。

sentences.en: How many beds, how many facilities, how many people would you say that you’re engaged in treating now?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 你们现在有多少床位、多少设施，大概正在为多少人提供治疗？

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, in Liberia, International Medical Corps opened up a 70-bed hospital —or actually we call it a treatment unit.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 在利比里亚，国际医疗队开办了一家有70张床位的医院——准确地说，我们称之为治疗中心。

sentences.en: We opened that up in mid-September.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 我们在九月中旬开始运营。

sentences.en: We are scaling up and we will be opening up another treatment unit in Sierra Leone.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 我们正在扩大规模，还将在塞拉利昂开设另一个治疗中心。

sentences.en: In Liberia, we have about 200 people working in this treatment unit, trying to contain it, as well as treating people who have Ebola, with the hopes that they will recover, and they are recovering when they receive treatment.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 在利比里亚，约有200人在这家治疗中心工作，努力遏制疫情，同时治疗埃博拉患者，希望他们能够康复；而患者接受治疗后也确实在逐渐康复。

sentences.en: Do you have any sense that the progress of this disease is being—is slowing?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 您是否感觉到，这种疾病的发展势头正在——正在减缓？

sentences.en: Well, let me say that it’s clear that efforts, like ours and other organizations’, are working.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 我想说，很明显，我们以及其他组织所作的努力正在发挥作用。

sentences.en: When there are treatment efforts, when there are health care workers to treat patients as they come in —I mean, our first patients that arrived to our treatment unit, they died at the doorstep.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 只要开展救治，只要有医护人员来接诊患者——我是说，最早来到我们治疗中心的那些患者，就倒在了门口。

sentences.en: But now we see that patients are recovering, and they’re returning back to their families.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 但现在，我们看到患者在康复，而且正在回归家庭。

sentences.en: So any efforts around treatment and containment are working.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 所以，围绕救治和控制疫情所作的努力都有效果。

sentences.en: The problem and the challenge is that there are just not enough operational efforts on the ground.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 问题和挑战在于，当地切实开展的救援行动还远远不够。

sentences.en: That’s the challenge.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 这就是面临的挑战。

sentences.en: Is that because a lack of international action or non-governmental action, or is it because the infrastructure in these communities is so difficult that even if you sent them 10 pop-up hospitals, they couldn’t build them?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 这是因为国际行动或非政府组织的行动不足，还是因为当地的基础设施条件太差，以至于即使送去十家临时医院，他们也无法建起来？

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, it’s a number of factors.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 原因有很多。

sentences.en: One, certainly, the health care infrastructures are very weak in West Africa, under-resourced.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 第一，西非的医疗基础设施确实非常薄弱，资源也很匮乏。

sentences.en: They don’t have enough health workers.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 他们没有足够的医护人员。

sentences.en: That’s one thing.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 这是其中一个原因。

sentences.en: The second thing is the spread wasn’t contained more quickly some months ago.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 第二，几个月前，疫情传播未能得到更迅速的控制。

sentences.en: International donors are stepping up.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 国际捐助方正在加大行动力度。

sentences.en: In fact, our treatment unit in Liberia was made possible from a grant from USAID’s Office of Foreign Disaster Assistance.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 实际上，我们在利比里亚的治疗中心得以建立，靠的是美国国际开发署海外灾难援助办公室的一笔拨款。

sentences.en: It took $5 million to open that up and about a million a month.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 建起这个中心花了500万美元，之后每个月大约还要100万美元。

sentences.en: So, part of it is the resources need to be there, but also people are really afraid.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 所以，一方面必须有资源支持，另一方面，人们也确实很害怕。

sentences.en: They’re afraid to provide treatment because they also need to keep their own health workers safe.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 他们不敢提供治疗，因为他们也必须保护自己医护人员的安全。

sentences.en: And so one of the things that we have done is we have said to other community health people as well as other international NGOs, we will provide case management protocol training.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 因此，我们采取的一项措施，就是告诉其他社区医护人员和国际非政府组织，我们将提供病例管理规范培训。

sentences.en: We will train their workers so that they can open up more treatment facilities.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 我们将培训他们的工作人员，让他们能够开设更多治疗设施。

sentences.en: The problem we have now is that the disease and the outbreak is being—is outpacing the operational efforts on ground.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 我们现在面临的问题是，疾病传播和疫情暴发的速度正在——正在超过当地救援行动的推进速度。

sentences.en: There are a lot of plans in place, by the way, to change that, and we’re still within that window.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，已经有许多计划在推进，以改变这种状况；而我们仍然处于能够采取行动的时机内。

w.m: n.可采取行动的时机；时间窗口

sentences.en: Well, Mary, thank you very much for staying with us today.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 玛丽，非常感谢您今天参加我们的节目。

sentences.en: You’re welcome.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 不客气。

sentences.en: This is the end of the first interview.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 第一段访谈到此结束。

sentences.en: Questions 1 to 5 are based on what you have just heard.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 第1至5题根据你刚才听到的内容提问。

sentences.en: Question 1. What is international leaders’ assessment of the current battle against Ebola?
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 第1题：国际领导人对当前抗击埃博拉疫情的形势作出了怎样的评估？

sentences.en: Question 2. How many people are now working in the treatment unit in Liberia?
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 第2题：目前有多少人在利比里亚的治疗中心工作？

sentences.en: Question 3. According to Mary, what is the challenge in the battle against Ebola?
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 第3题：据玛丽所说，抗击埃博拉疫情面临的挑战是什么？

sentences.en: Question 4. Why do health workers need case management protocol training?
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 第4题：为什么医护人员需要接受病例管理规范培训？

sentences.en: Question 5. What does this interview mainly talk about?
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 第5题：这段访谈主要谈论什么？

sentences.en: Now, listen to the second interview.
sentences.zh: 现在请听第二段访谈。

sentences.en: Questions 6 to 10 are based on the second interview.
sentences.zh: 第6至10题根据第二段访谈提问。

sentences.en: Tom, I understand that when Havas Media North America hired you early this year to be head of strategy and innovation, it did not include the words “future” or “futurist” in your title, but a large part of your role is understanding where the near- and not-so-distant futures of media can be applied and accelerated in ways that give Havas and its clients a competitive advantage.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我了解到，Havas Media北美公司今年年初聘请你担任战略与创新主管时，你的职位名称并没有包含“未来”或“未来学家”这样的词；但你的工作很大一部分，是理解如何应用和加速推进媒体近期以及更远一些的未来发展，为Havas及其客户带来竞争优势。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: What exactly is your role at Havas?
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 那么，你在Havas的具体职责是什么？

sentences.en: Well, I’m very lucky in that I get paid to think!
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 我很幸运，因为我可以靠思考来领薪水！

sentences.en: My role is about understanding the changes in behavior, technology and media, and then to use that information to inspire new thinking and new ideas, and then to bring them to life.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 我的职责是了解行为、技术和媒体的变化，再利用这些信息激发新的思考和创意，并把它们变成现实。

sentences.en: It could be anything from what the internet of things means for our clients to how mobile coupons could develop.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 这可能涉及任何事情，从物联网对客户意味着什么，到移动优惠券将如何发展。

sentences.en: The key is making something from it.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 关键是要从中创造出实际的东西。

sentences.en: What areas of the business do you think require the most focus on innovation right now?
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 你认为，目前业务的哪些方面最需要聚焦创新？

sentences.en: I think we need to innovate in two very broad areas.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 我认为，我们需要在两个大的方面进行创新。

sentences.en: First, we need to start working around people and not our own interests or channels.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 首先，我们应该围绕人来开展工作，而不是围绕自身利益或传播渠道。

sentences.en: We need to create new processes and structures, and bring in new talent to take advantage of the evolving media landscape.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 我们需要建立新的流程和架构，引进新人才，抓住不断变化的媒体环境所带来的机会。

sentences.en: In the same way that television shows were plays that were filmed, we’ve tended to simply repurpose advertising units that were invented several decades ago.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 就像早期电视节目只是把舞台剧拍下来一样，我们往往只是把几十年前发明的广告形式重新拿来使用。

sentences.en: Secondly, we need to re-evaluate the role of advertising.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 其次，我们需要重新评估广告的作用。

sentences.en: For me, media agencies should not be advising clients on how to spend marketing money, but applying design thinking, creativity, data and consumer understanding to solve client business problems.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 在我看来，媒体代理公司不应该只是建议客户如何花营销预算，而应该运用设计思维、创造力、数据和对消费者的理解，解决客户的商业问题。

sentences.en: How do you know which areas to focus on that will actually lead to business results vs. being interesting, but potentially low-yielding dead-ends?
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 你如何判断哪些方向真正能带来业务成效，而不只是看起来有趣、实际却可能回报很低、走不通的方向？

w.m: n.死胡同；无发展前景的方向

sentences.en: The hardest thing with innovation is that it needs people to take a risk.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 创新最困难的地方在于，它需要人们承担风险。

sentences.en: You can’t do anything for the first time if you need to show previous success stories, because by definition it’s never been done before.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 如果非得先拿出以往的成功案例，你就无法首次尝试任何事情，因为按定义来说，它以前从未有人做过。

sentences.en: As an industry, we need to focus on our gut feelings and on superb ideas, not just data supported arguments.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 作为一个行业，我们需要关注直觉和出色的创意，而不能只看有数据支持的论证。

sentences.en: What areas do you think are being overlooked by the industry that could be game-changing opportunities in the future?
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 你认为，行业目前忽略了哪些领域，而这些领域未来可能成为改变格局的机会？

sentences.en: I believe that the industry is going to start targeting at a user level, serving messages directly to consumers.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 我相信，这个行业将开始直接在用户层面精准触达，把信息直接传递给消费者。

sentences.en: Right now, we still move people to visit websites or enter some silly competition.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 现在，我们仍然把人们引导到网站上，或让他们参加某些无聊的竞赛。

sentences.en: Why not use ads to download mobile coupons or send offers to friends, or save locations to bookmark, or make phone calls?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 为什么不利用广告下载移动优惠券、把优惠信息发给朋友、收藏地点，或者直接打电话呢？

sentences.en: How do you reconcile your role between innovating and applying it into strategy?
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 你如何协调创新与把创新应用到战略之中的职责？

sentences.en: The hardest part of my job is establishing the “focal point.”
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 我工作中最难的部分，是确立“着力点”。

sentences.en: My approach is first to take a long hard look at the future and see what will be possible one day, and then to consider an entry point that is buyable in the next 4 months, and make it happen.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 我的做法是，先认真审视未来，看看有朝一日什么能够实现；再考虑一个未来四个月内有望获得买单支持的切入点，并将它落实。

sentences.en: What do you think of other agencies getting directly into the ventures game to fuel innovation vis-à-vis capital, or is it best left to professional venture capital firms, or clients to do directly?
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 你怎么看待其他代理公司直接参与风险投资，以资本来推动创新？或者，这类事情最好还是交给专业风投公司，或由客户自己直接去做？

sentences.en: I think the role of media agencies needs to be about collaboration and openness and fostering creativity, but the key is how that is done, and how we ensure that everything is about the best interests of our clients.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 我认为，媒体代理公司的职责应当体现合作、开放以及对创造力的培育；但关键在于怎样实现这些目标，以及怎样确保一切都以客户的最大利益为出发点。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Tom, thanks for being with us.
sentences.speaker: W
sentences.zh: 汤姆，谢谢你参加我们的节目。

sentences.en: Pleasure.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 很高兴来参加。

w.m: n.乐意；此处用于客气回应

sentences.en: This is the end of the second interview.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 第二段访谈到此结束。

sentences.en: Questions 6 to 10 are based on what you have just heard.
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 第6至10题根据你刚才听到的内容提问。

sentences.en: Question 6. What is Tom’s main role in his new position?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 第6题：汤姆在新职位上的主要职责是什么？

sentences.en: Question 7. According to Tom, what does innovation require of people?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 第7题：根据汤姆的说法，创新需要人们做到什么？

sentences.en: Question 8. What does Tom see as game-changing chances in the future?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 第8题：汤姆认为，哪些机会未来可能改变行业格局？

sentences.en: Question 9. What does Tom do first to deal with the toughest part of his work?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 第9题：为了解决工作中最棘手的部分，汤姆首先会做什么？

sentences.en: Question 10. Which of the following might Tom work for?
sentences.speaker: M
sentences.zh: 第10题：汤姆可能为以下哪类机构工作？
